exercises.title: Schematic Capture and Documentation: concept check
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Which practice makes a schematic reviewable by another engineer?
choices: Relying on the PCB artwork to show connectivity
Meaningful net names, labelled rails, notes on design intent, datasheet-based part data, and a clean ERC
Hiding connector pin assignments in the BOM
hints: A schematic should explain intent without the layout.

exercises.title: Schematic Capture and Documentation: worked analysis
exercises.instructionMarkdown:
Review a deliberately flawed schematic and produce a corrected block, BOM notes, and test-point plan.

Show assumptions, equations, units, standard-value choices, ratings, tolerance effects, and the measurements that would verify the result.
checklist: I drew or described the complete source and return path.
I carried units and checked the order of magnitude.
I checked ratings and at least one worst-case condition.
I wrote an observable verification step before viewing the solution.
hints: Start with a symbolic relationship before substituting numbers.
Separate typical behavior from guaranteed limits and add measurement tolerance.
exercises.solutionMarkdown:
## Reference solution

The corrected schematic uses unique references, explicit connector pin numbers, net names that express function, visible supply and return intent, polarity and rating notes, decoupling at each IC, protection at external connectors, and test points on every rail and critical interface. ERC exceptions are documented rather than globally suppressed.

The governing principle is: **make intent reviewable by another engineer without relying on memory or PCB artwork**. Define every reference direction and convert values to coherent SI units. Compare the result with component ratings and standard available values, then report a bounded expectation that includes tolerance, temperature, supply variation, and instrument loading.

### Verification evidence

1. Power off and confirm wiring, polarity, and discharge state.
2. Configure a conservative current limit.
3. Predict source current and the critical node voltages or waveform features.
4. Power on and compare the first measurement with the bounded prediction.
5. Stop if current, temperature, smell, or waveform exceeds the safe bound.

The notebook should make both the reasoning and bench test independently reproducible.

exercises.title: Schematic Capture and Documentation: measurement and fault investigation
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Plan or perform a low-voltage investigation of **hidden power pin, ambiguous connector, missing ratings, inconsistent net names**. Record a safe setup, predicted healthy evidence, observed evidence, one hypothesis at a time, and the final verification.
checklist: I documented the de-energized inspection and safe current limit.
I recorded expected healthy readings before measuring.
I used one falsifiable hypothesis at a time.
I included final evidence that distinguishes cause from symptom.
hints: Measure the supply current and block boundaries before probing internal details.
Change only one condition between measurements.
